column1: # Where this launcher answers a range differently from npm, and why.
# Every line is a case npm answers one way and this launcher answers the other, from the two files
# named in npm-satisfies.tsv. They are of two kinds, labelled below: a **decision** is a difference
# this launcher made on purpose, and a **gap** is one it has not made yet. The test that reads this
# fails if the list changes in either direction — a case that starts agreeing has to be struck off,
# and one that stops agreeing is a difference nobody wrote down — so the gaps can only shrink.
# Each line is: which way it is wrong, the range, the version.

# GAPS — differences this launcher has not made yet. They may only shrink.
#   build metadata is not part of what a version means
#     npm ignores everything from + on when it decides whether a version fits; this launcher compares
#     the text, so 1.2.3 does not fit ^1.2.3+build.
#   the operator and its version may be separated by whitespace
#     npm reads >= 1.0.0, <= 2.0.0, a tab after < and ~ 1.0. This launcher reads none of them, so a
#     plugin whose range is written that way is hidden from every instance.
#   a partial version above the bound
#     >1.2 is past everything in the 1.2 line, so npm answers that 1.2.8 does not fit; this launcher
#     npm accepts it, this launcher does not.
#     npm reads =0.7.x, <=0.7.x and <=7.x; this launcher reads the .x as text. A bare 1.x it does
#   a pre-release fits a range that does not name one
#     The harness installs a plugin by asking npm with includePrerelease, so a bound that names no
#     pre-release is about the numbers alone. Reading npm's default rule instead turned away every
#     plugin declaring >=0.1.0-rc.0 <0.2.0, the commonest range of all. npm's own fixtures answer the
#     same way wherever they mark an entry includePrerelease.
#     npm resolves an empty string to *, everything. This launcher reads it as a requirement nothing
#     fits: a plugin with an empty entry says nothing about the harness rather than asking for all of
#   the version compared against is always a version
#     An invalid version fits nothing, not even *. What this launcher compares against is read from
#     the instance's own installation, so the case cannot arise rather than being handled.
